target_customer: Originally Medicare care management programs; the current website instead targets skilled nursing facilities buying an outsourced business office
problem: Remote follow up and monitoring of older Medicare patients is labor heavy; the later site describes skilled nursing facilities losing money to overcharges and missed reimbursement.
business_model: AI plus services; per the current site, recovery of money on behalf of facilities (fee basis not stated)
product_category: AI care management, later AI back office for nursing facilities

founders.name: Peter Chien
founders.background_notes: YC page: led neurosurgical robotics sensors, algorithms and mechanisms at Neuralink; 600+ hours of field work in hospitals and senior communities.

founders.name: Lukas Klaiber
founders.background_notes: Research at Stanford CDR per the YC page.

founders.name: Kazuki Shin
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, has published 12 IEEE papers.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents for phone calls with older patients, plus aggregating voice biomarkers and monitoring data, were feasible with 2025 voice AI APIs but need healthcare compliance; the team has robotics, ML and software backgrounds per the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: Voice agent components were commodity APIs in 2025; no data or regulatory moat was shown in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other AI voice care management startups existed by the time of coverage (a search summary cites Ellipsis Health raising $45M and Popai), but those sources were undated, so they are not listed as competitors at founding. No incumbent action against Kaigo found.

market_need_then: CMS chronic care and remote monitoring programs pay for care management, and phone calls suit older patients. A search summary says CMS launched the ACCESS model in July 2026, later than founding.

branding.domain_note: kaigohealth.ai is the company domain; no purchase story found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: A design agency portfolio claims it made a trustworthy, accessible identity; self promotional
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, punchy and action focused, with occasional emojis, per the company site

branding.brand_signature: Tagline We find it. We get it back. on the current site
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found. An unrelated earlier Kaigo Health app with Mount Sinai was reported in 2016.

brand_strength.rationale: Kaigo is the Japanese word for nursing care (a search result said so; the founders did not state the intent), which fits the elder care focus, but an older unrelated Kaigo Health app exists and no press covers the brand.

pivots.from: AI outpatient care management for Medicare patients via phone calls
pivots.to: Outsourced business office for skilled nursing facilities recovering lost money
pivots.why: Not stated; the current website describes the new business while the YC page still describes the old one. Date approximate.

outcome_analysis: Kaigo Health is active and early, with a three person team from Neuralink, NVIDIA and SAP backgrounds. Its website now describes a different business than the YC listing, which suggests a pivot toward nursing facility back office work. No funding beyond the standard YC deal and no exit were found, so the story is too early to read.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators report $500,000 from YC (a founder LinkedIn post from October 2025 per a search summary); one aggregator headline says $1M with no support. No round recorded. Competitor search returned only undated sources, so the list is empty. Name origin not stated by the company. Pivot date approximate and inferred from the website differing from the YC page.
